91: ### Event Fact Structure
92: Each EventFact represents a discrete, ordered lifecycle occurrence:
93: - timestamp: ISO 8601 formatted timestamp string in UTC (microsecond precision).
94: - session_id: Unique identifier of the session where the event occurred.
95: - turn: Sequential 1-based turn number within the session.
96: - role: Agent role associated with the session (e.g. orchestrator, planner, coder, tester, reviewer).
97: - event_type: Categorical identifier (tool_call, turn_message, compaction).
98: - tool_name: Optional string containing the tool name (e.g. bash, read, edit, grep, write), present for tool calls.
99: - status: Execution status string (e.g. completed, error).
100: - error_message: Optional string containing the error excerpt if the event encountered an error.
101: - duration_ms: Optional int64 measuring execution duration in milliseconds.
102: - context_tokens: Cumulative context token volume (input tokens plus cache read tokens) at the point of the event.
103: 
104: ### Chronological Correlation Algorithm
105: 1. Query session records for target root threads and child invocations, establishing session role and model mapping.
106: 2. Query message records for all sessions ordered by creation timestamp:
107:    - Assign sequential 1-based turn numbers to messages within each session.
108:    - Extract input and cache tokens to compute context_tokens.
109:    - Generate turn_message event facts.
110: 3. Query part records for all sessions ordered by creation timestamp:
111:    - For parts where data LIKE '%"type":"tool"%':
112:      - Parse tool name, state status, and output.

118:    - For parts where data LIKE '%"type":"compaction"%':
119:      - Correlate turn index from parent message ID.
120:      - Generate compaction event facts.
121: 4. Merge all extracted events into a single slice.
122: 5. Sort chronologically by timestamp in ascending order, using turn as secondary tie-breaker.
